title: Paul tells his story (Acts 22)
hook: arrested, he asks to speak and tells of Damascus in Hebrew
tomorrow: men swear not to eat until Paul is dead. who overhears?

segments.voice: Agabus and the belt: a true warning, and friends who said, the will of the Lord be done. Paul reaches Jerusalem, and the warning comes true fast.
screen: `THE WILL OF THE LORD BE DONE.` → `IN JERUSALEM, IT COMES TRUE.`

segments.voice: Job interviews, college essays, first dates: sooner or later someone says, so, tell me about yourself. Paul gets that question in a setting nobody would choose. Roman soldiers have just pulled him out of a crowd at the temple and are carrying him up the steps of the castle, as the King James calls their fortress. Halfway up, he asks the commander one thing: let me speak to the people. He turns, raises his hand, and when they hear him speak in the Hebrew tongue, Acts says "they kept the more silence." And he tells them a story.
screen: `SO, TELL ME ABOUT YOURSELF.` → `UP THE CASTLE STAIRS.` → `THEY KEPT THE MORE SILENCE.`

segments.voice: He doesn't open with an argument. He opens with who he is: "I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel." He admits the worst part plainly: he once hunted down people who followed this way. Then the road to Damascus, about noon. "Suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me." He falls, and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" He answers, "Who art thou, Lord?" and the reply comes: "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest." Then his second question, the one today's line comes from: "What shall I do, Lord?" Not why me. Not prove it. What shall I do. He's led by the hand into Damascus, unable to see, and a devout man named Ananias stands by him and says, "Brother Saul, receive thy sight." That's the whole shape: who he was, what happened, who helped, what he asked. One to tell a friend tonight: the turning point of the story is a question. The crowd listens until he says he's been sent to the Gentiles, and the shouting starts again. So what does this give you for the next time someone says, tell me about yourself? Say it plainly. Name who helped. Leave the polish out.
screen: `WHO HE WAS: AT GAMALIEL'S FEET.` · `A GREAT LIGHT AT NOON.` · `BROTHER SAUL, RECEIVE THY SIGHT.` · `SAY IT PLAINLY.` · then, large: `WHAT SHALL I DO, LORD?`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write your own story in three short lines: who I was, what happened, what I'm asking now. Keep it plain; nobody will read it but you. If you pray, you can end with Paul's question: what shall I do, Lord?
Paul tells his story. On the castle stairs, in the Hebrew tongue: who he was, what happened, who helped, and what he asked.
Your line: what shall I do, Lord? It was Paul's second question, and the one that changed his road. See you tomorrow.

chat.meaning: Paul told it plainly: who he was, what happened, who helped him, and what he asked. A plain, true story is enough.

Tarsus.meaning: Paul's hometown, a city in Cilicia

Gamaliel.meaning: a respected teacher of the law in Jerusalem

Damascus.meaning: the city Paul was traveling to when the light came

Ananias.meaning: a devout man in Damascus who helped Paul see again
